issue_context.title: gRPC library doesn't support local credentials with Python custom IO managers
issue_context.body:

-->

### What version of gRPC and what language are you using?

gRPC: Current code in master 
Language: Python

### What operating system (Linux, Windows,...) and version?

Linux

### What runtime / compiler are you using (e.g. python version or version of gcc)

Whatever is used when running `tools/run_tests/run_tests.py use_docker`.
Container image is `python_stretch_default_x64_c89a739b8ceabb422409a4475cd68b3e457eb622`.

### What did you do?

Run unit tests from 'unit._local_credentials_test.LocalCredentialsTest' for the eventlet custom IO manager I'm working on, but it should be the same with the other custom IO managers.

### What did you expect to see?

Local credentials should be supported for custom IO managers and unit tests for that specific test class should pass.

### What did you see instead?

Test failure with error: `Endpoint is neither UDS or TCP loopback address.`

As far as I looked, this is because the `local_check_peer` function in `src/core/lib/security/security_connector/local/local_security_connector.cc` relies on getting the fd with `grpc_endpoint_get_fd` and then getting the sock name for it with `getsockname`, but for custom IO managers it won't work, because  `endpoint_get_fd` returns -1.

For custom managers the code should probably use a different mechanism to get the sockname, for example directly using `getsockname` method from the `grpc_socket_vtable`.
comments: @lidizheng This is working in the asyncio stack, isn't it?

@gnossen Thanks for the quick reply.
Using a local IP (v4 or v6) doesn't solve the issue:
```
I0218 15:51:14.116180682   20948 handshaker.cc:178]          handshake_manager 0x55aa7a3d64e0: calling handshaker security [0x55aa7a3d60b0] at index 1                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
D0218 15:51:14.116193719   20948 security_handshaker.cc:184] Security handshake failed: {"created":"@1582037474.116185457","description":"Endpoint is neither UDS or TCP loopback address.","file":"src/core/lib/security/security_connector/local/local_security_connector.cc","file_line":110}                                                                                                                                         
I0218 15:51:14.116199235   20948 tcp_custom.cc:290]          TCP 0x55aa7a3735a0 shutdown why={"created":"@1582037474.116185457","description":"Endpoint is neither UDS or TCP loopback address.","file":"src/core/lib/security/security_connector/local/local_security_connector.cc","file_line":110}                                                                                                                                    
I0218 15:51:14.116226841   20948 handshaker.cc:131]          handshake_manager 0x55aa7a3d64e0: error={"created":"@1582037474.116185457","description":"Endpoint is neither UDS or TCP loopback address.","file":"src/core/lib/security/security_connector/local/local_security_connector.cc","file_line":110} shutdown=0 index=2, args={endpoint=(nil), args=(nil) {size=0: (null)}, read_buffer=(nil) (length=0), exit_early=0}         
```

The other day when I looked at this with GDB I was able to confirm that the first issue (there may be more) is in the the `local_check_peer`, because it gets -1 when retrieving the endpoint's fd.

This happens because in `src/core/lib/iomgr/tcp_custom.cc` we have this code:
```
static int endpoint_get_fd(grpc_endpoint* /*ep*/) { return -1; }
```

And since `local_check_peer` only tries to get the sockname using the returned fd, then it fails.

I believe asyncio should also fail, because I didn't see it changing the get_fd method in any way, though I could be wrong.

review_comments: Instead of logging, please have this function return an `absl::Status`, so that we can indicate the failure to the caller.  The caller can decide to log if it wants to.

These two includes should go above the absl include on line 23, in their own section.

https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html#Names_and_Order_of_Includes
Please put this in the `grpc_core` namespace and call it `UriStringToSockaddr()`.
No need to convert from `absl::string_view` to `std::string` (which makes a needless copy) to `char*` and back to `absl::string_view` here.  Just pass `peer_address` as-is.
This check is missing from the new code.
Good catch. I thought this check will be enforced in other places, but this turned out to be the only place checking `grpc_local_connect_type`.
If this fails, let's return a not-OK status instead of just populating the address with all-zero.
